title: France Startup Day — launch messaging & competitive brief (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working draft for PR/announce copy and sales enablement for our presence at France Startup Day (Paris). Target: early-stage French startups + startup-focused VCs exploring native LLM features and predictable inference economics.

Audience and goals (primary):
- Founders & engineers at startups (Series A–C) who care about latency, predictability, and cost control when shipping LLM features.
- Platform/infra leads at startups who want a path from prototype (hosted) to predictable production (dedicated/private).
- VC/partner scouts interested in partner opportunities.
Goals: drive demo signups, secure 25 workshop attendees, and 5 qualified leads for Dedicated trials in Q1.

Key single-line message (working):
Ship powerful LLM features without the inference guesswork — Redwood gives predictable performance, transparent cost levers, and a simple path from API to dedicated capacity.

Three pillar messaging (for use in 60s talk and booth):
1) Predictable economics for product teams — clear knobs (batching, quantization, caching) that actually move the unit cost needle.
2) Production-first runtime — low-latency serving, transparent SLOs, and graceful fallback to keep customer UX alive.
3) Deploy everywhere on your terms — hosted API to get started, dedicated capacity for scale, private for regulated/data-sensitive apps.

Feature emphasis for this audience:
- Fast prototype to production: same API for hosted -> dedicated -> private (no refactor).
- Developer ergonomics: SDKs in Python/TS, example templates for chat, search, summarization.
- Cost/playbook: recommended profiles (small chatbot vs high-throughput embedding pipeline) with expected $/k token ranges and latency bands.

Competitive framing (notes / quick soundbites):
- vs. Big cloud managed endpoints (GCP/Vertex, AWS Sagemaker): emphasize inference economics and routing policies — we give lower-cost options and predictable unit pricing rather than opaque provisioning tied to VM types.
- vs. LLM API players (OpenAI, Anthropic): emphasize deployment flexibility + deterministic performance at scale (dedicated pools, SLAs), and stronger observability (+rollouts tied to evals).
- vs. self-hosted runtimes (Replicate, private stacks): we offer the same control with a managed ops surface (autoscaling, kernel selection, KMS) and lower operational burden.

Proof points to cite (short):
- 2–3x cost reduction example with batching + prefix cache on long-context search workload (internal benchmark, q3).
- 99.9% availability on Dedicated customers in last 90 days (anonymized).
- Case snippet: "Fintech startup lowered median generation latency from 420ms to 120ms by switching to dedicated optimized runtime" (contact: Solutions Eng).

Sample announcement copy (short, social/booth friendly):
Headline: Build LLM features that scale in the real world.
Blurb: At France Startup Day — meet Redwood to learn how teams move from prototype to production without surprise bills or flaky inference. Demos all day.
Call to action: Scan our QR for a workshop seat and a free Dedicated trial review.

Sales enablement bullets (for booth + SDRs):
- Lead qualifier questions: (1) current model provider? (2) tokens/day today vs target? (3) latency targets for product? (4) regulatory or data residency concerns?
- For prototypes: pitch hosted API + quickstart templates and 30-minute integration session.
- For scale prospects: highlight Dedicated (predictable throughput, commit options) + Private (VPC/HSM).

Objections & quick counters: 
- "We're on OpenAI and it's easy" -> Counter: ease to prototype is real; Redwood shortens the path to predictable production without duplicating integration work — same API, fallback routing, and transparent cost levers.
- "We're worried about model quality" -> Counter: model catalog with verified perf profiles + rollout/eval tooling to prevent regressions. Offer to run a short head-to-head on our demo dataset.
- "We manage our own infra" -> Counter: if you want control without the ops tax, Dedicated + Private give control + managed autoscaling, kernel tuning and SRE ops.

Event enablement checklist (owner initials):
- Deck: 5-slide product narrative + demo script (A. Chen)
- Demo env: hosted demo tokens rotated + sample dataset in FR (L. Müller)
- Booth one-pager (FR + EN) + QR code to signup (D. Ramos)
- SDR outreach playbook for post-event follow-ups (S. Bernard)
- Case study short (anonymized) to hand to prospects who ask for evidence (PMM)

Open questions (to resolve before final):
- French translations: full one-pager vs minimal FR key bullets? (need ops estimate)
- Pricing language in one-pager: publish ranges or invite to trial/assessment? (legal + finance)
- Workshop capacity: what is our follow-up SLA to attendees (response time / qualification flow)?

Timeline (draft):
- 2024-12-05: Finalize copy + FR localization
- 2024-12-12: Print one-pagers and upload assets to shared drive
- 2024-12-17: Rehearse demo + SDR playbook dry run
- 2025-01-09: France Startup Day (follow-ups start day after)

Appendix / quick talk outline (90s):
- Hook (20s): "We help teams stop guessing about inference — predictable latency, predictable costs."
- Problem (20s): "Prototypes become costly & flaky at scale; teams re-architect or overprovision."
- Solution (30s): "Redwood: runtime + routing + deployment choices. One API, clear knobs, measurable unit economics."
- Close (20s): "Book our 30-min workshop to see where you can save 30–50% on serving costs and cut median latency in half."

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep claims narrowly scoped — legal will push back on % savings without clear benchmark definitions.
- Need FR speaker notes for demo engineer (short sentences).
- Follow up with Solutions Eng to lock anonymized case study quote.
